title: release: micropatch manifest sharding, timestamped rotation, and fast rollback indexer
author: Priya Nambiar
description: Motivation: shipping private-installer updates to customers currently requires building large TUF release bundles which slows rollouts and makes quick rollbacks cumbersome. This PR introduces a micropatch manifest sharder and timestamped rotation scheme plus a fast rollback indexer so we can publish small delta manifests for urgent fixes and recoveries. The changeset includes: 1) a new release manifest "micropatch" format (JSON schema v1.2) that references sharded artifact groups and includes per-shard provenance entries, 2) a rotation controller that stamps manifests with RFC3339 timestamps and KMS-signed miniroots using Cosign-compatible attestation, 3) an indexer that builds a compact rollback index allowing O(1) selection of the last known-good micropatch per-customer segment, 4) Terraform module pins for the private-installer infra modules to ensure deterministic image and chart pins during rollout, 5) Helm chart bump and compatibility adaptors to support micropatch strategy during upgrades, 6) CI pipeline additions to produce and validate micropatch artifacts and run an e2e smoke test against an airgapped fkci grid. Backwards compatibility: the installer continues to accept legacy release bundles; the launcher will prefer micropatch manifests when present. Rollout plan: canary micropatches to 5% of dedicated accounts, monitor Canary SLOs and rollout to 100% in 24h unless regressions reported. Checklist: [x] manifest schema and validator, [x] cosign attestation integration, [x] terraform pinning, [x] helm adaptor, [x] indexer CLI and tests, [x] pipeline integration and gating. Related: ENG-1187 for micropatch design, SUP-3421 customer incident that motivated faster rollback paths.
